current.title: Monthly CA filing system
explain: Keep eight hanging folders: Polity, Economy, IR, Environment, S&T, Security, Social justice, Bihar. Every clipping gets a date, a 40-word gist, and a syllabus tag.
Sunday review: drop anything you cannot explain aloud. Add one map and one ethics dilemma from the week’s news.

current.title: Issue note template (one page)
explain: Header: issue + paper (GS-II/III) + Bihar/national. Body: what happened, why now, stakeholders, constitutional or scheme hook, two-sided argument, way forward with an institution named.
If you cannot name a body (EC, RBI, NDMA, NGT, Finance Commission), the note is still journalism, not GS.

current.title: IR and security from the same newspaper
explain: Neighbourhood first: Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar, China, Pakistan — one line each on the live file. Then QUAD, BRICS, UN, WTO only if the story actually moved.
Internal security: Left-wing extremism, border management, cyber, money trails. Do not mix a crime report with a GS-III answer unless a policy lever exists.

current.title: Bihar CA shortlist
explain: Floods and rivers, education exams, health (kala-azar, AES belts), migration and jobs, agriculture (makhana, litchi, maize), and any CAG/assembly story on delivery. That is enough for BPSC if revised monthly.
Quote a number only if you can source it (Economic Survey of Bihar, NFHS, Census, IMD).

history.title: Timeline drill (must recite)
explain: Harappa → mahajanapadas → Maurya → Gupta → regional kingdoms → Sultanate → Mughals → 18th-century states → Company → 1857 → Congress → Gandhi → 1947 → Constitution. If the spine is firm, facts hang on it.
Add Bihar beads on the same thread: Magadha, Nalanda, Sher Shah, 1857, Champaran, 1942, post-2005 governance as contemporary history of the state.

history.title: Art and culture in four boxes
explain: Architecture (stupa, temple Nagara–Dravida–Vesara, Indo-Islamic, colonial), sculpture and painting (Ajanta, Chola bronze, Mughal, Patna Kalam), literature and philosophy (Vedanta, Bhakti–Sufi, modern print), performing arts (classical dance/music families, folk of Bihar: Madhubani, Sonepur, Bidesia).
Prelims wants a feature + dynasty/region. Mains wants what the art says about patronage and society.

history.title: Modern India economic spine
explain: Drain, deindustrialisation, land systems, railways and irrigation as extraction plus modernisation, commercialisation of agriculture, famines as political economy, early Indian capital (Bombay mills, Marwari networks).
This block writes half of GS-I modern and feeds GS-III agriculture/industry answers.

history.title: Freedom struggle social map
explain: Do not write only Gandhi. Keep workers, peasants, tribals, women, depressed classes, revolutionaries, INA, and the communal question on one page with one example each.
Bihar: Champaran, peasant satyagrahas, 1942, Kunwar Singh as 1857 memory.

history.title: Post-independence (GS-I)
explain: Integration of states, linguistic reorganisation, planned economy, Green Revolution, 1975–77 as constitutional stress, Mandal, coalition era, liberalisation 1991. Keep it analytical and dated, not partisan.
Link each to a polity or economy chapter so the same fact is not rewritten three times.

geography.title: Atlas hour
explain: Thirty minutes, three maps: India rivers, India soils/rainfall, world currents or plates. Tracing by hand beats highlighting PDFs.
Then write four lines: process, Indian example, disaster or economy link, a newspaper hook.

geography.title: Monsoon one-diagram
explain: Onset: ITCZ shift, Tibetan heat, Somali jet, Bay and Arabian branches. Breaks: subtropical westerly jet and monsoon trough position. Retreat: beginning of cyclonic window in the Bay.
ENSO and IOD are modulators. Never say ‘El Niño means drought always’ — say probability and regional exception.

geography.title: Resources without shopping lists
explain: For coal, iron, petroleum, rare earths, solar: location, grade/constraint, environment cost, logistics, and a policy (auction, just transition, critical minerals).
Bihar’s mineral story is mostly next door (Jharkhand) plus the state’s own mica/limestone pockets — say that honestly.

geography.title: Human geography for Mains
explain: Density, sex ratio, literacy, urbanisation, migration (push–pull, remittances), slums, industrial location (Weber flavour without the jargon). Census themes beat random district lists.
Bihar out-migration is a complete GS-I/III answer if you add destination, skill, social cost, and a state skill/urban policy.

geography.title: Disaster geography
explain: Hazard vs vulnerability vs capacity. Floods of North Bihar, drought south of Ganga fringe, earthquakes in Himalayan belt, heat, lightning. Structural (embankment, reservoir) vs non-structural (warning, insurance, land use).
Sendai and NDMA are the institutional overlay; science is still the map.

polity.title: Article clusters to own
explain: Do not mug 395 articles. Own clusters: Preamble; 12–35 rights; 36–51 DPSPs; Union executive; Parliament; judiciary; federal (246, 263, 280, 356); local government 73–74; emergency; amendment 368.
For each cluster keep one case (Kesavananda, Minerva Mills, S.R. Bommai, K.S. Puttaswamy, etc.) and one current news item.

polity.title: Bihar governance file
explain: Panchayats, public service delivery, flood administration, education exams, and police as GS-II examples. Stay institutional, not partisan.

polity.title: Constitutional, statutory, regulatory
explain: Write a 3-column table: EC/CAG/UPSC/FC vs NHRC/CIC/Lokpal vs SEBI/RBI/CCI/TRAI. Appointment, removal, one function, one controversy.
Prelims loves the column; Mains loves independence vs accountability.

polity.title: Rights that grew after 1950
explain: Article 21 as a tree: due process flavour, privacy, environment, health, education (also 21A), legal aid, speedy trial. RTI, NFSA, Forest Rights as statutory cousins.
Reasonable restrictions and national security are the other side of the same note.

polity.title: Parliament that actually works
explain: Question Hour, zero hour flavour, standing and departmentally related committees, money vs ordinary vs constitution amendment bills, ordinance route, anti-defection’s effect on debate.
Decline of deliberation is a Mains theme; committees are the constructive paragraph.

economy.title: Survey–Budget ritual
explain: After the Economic Survey, lift ten facts that illustrate a concept you already know (inflation, jobs, agriculture, inequality). After the Budget, lift the fiscal math and three scheme redesigns. Do not photocopy the whole documents.

economy.title: Inflation and the poor
explain: CPI vs WPI, food vs core, rural vs urban. Monetary tightening cools demand; food inflation often needs supply (buffer, logistics, weather). Say who is hurt: wage lag, real interest, fiscal subsidy bill.
Never write ‘RBI should cut GST’ — wrong instrument.

economy.title: Banking and inclusion
explain: Commercial banks, RRBs, cooperative stress, NBFCs, payment banks. NPAs, PCA, IBC. Inclusion: PMJDY, UPI, credit to MSME and farmers, insurance/pension (PMJJBY, APY).
Digital is not inclusion if last-mile grievance and connectivity fail — a Bihar-relevant sentence.

economy.title: Agriculture for two papers
explain: MSP, APMC, e-NAM, FPOs, food Corporation, NFSA, crop insurance, irrigation (AIBP flavour), climate risk. Bihar: small holdings, floods, horticulture, makhana GI-type stories, migration of labour.
WTO: public stockholding and special safeguard — one paragraph, not a treatise.

economy.title: External sector in five numbers
explain: Merchandise deficit vs services surplus, CAD, forex, FDI vs FPI, rupee. Then one risk: oil, global rates, or a FTA.
Remittances are a Bihar–Kerala–Punjab human story sitting inside BoP.

science.title: School science recovery list
explain: Light, electricity, carbon compounds, human physiology, reproduction, environment in Class 10 NCERT. One week of honest NCERT beats six coaching PDFs.
Then add a current file: space, health, digital public infrastructure, biotech regulation.

science.title: Space applications, not nicknames
explain: Launchers (PSLV/GSLV/SSLV flavour), Earth observation, NavIC, disaster, agriculture, communication. Gaganyaan as human-space capability plus industrial ecosystem.
Write: what data, who uses it (IMD, agriculture, NDMA), what equity issue (connectivity of poor districts).

science.title: Health S&T
explain: Vaccines, diagnostics, AMR, vector control (kala-azar, JE/AES in eastern plains), nutrition science vs food policy, telemedicine. One Health: human–animal–environment.
Regulation: CDSCO, ICMR, vaccine trials ethics.

science.title: Digital public infrastructure
explain: Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, ONDC flavour, data empowerment. Gains: inclusion, leak-proof DBT. Risks: exclusion errors, surveillance, cyber, consent.
Data protection law + CERT-In + critical information infrastructure = GS-III internal security as well.

science.title: Energy tech
explain: Solar, wind, storage, green hydrogen (electrolyser + water + offtake honesty), nuclear three-stage flavour, ethanol blending, semiconductors as strategic manufacturing.
Every tech needs grid, minerals, and just transition for coal districts.

environment.title: Convention one-pagers
explain: UNFCCC, CBD, CITES, Ramsar, CMS, Stockholm, Basel, Montreal. For each: year, aim, India angle, a current COP or listing in the news.

environment.title: India’s PA and species file
explain: Project Tiger/Elephant, biospheres, Ramsar in the Ganga basin, vulture decline, Gangetic dolphin as a Bihar–UP river flagship, grassland vs plantation mistakes.
Corridors and human–wildlife conflict are the Mains paragraphs; lists of parks are Prelims only.

environment.title: Pollution instruments
explain: Command-and-control (standards, closure) vs market (ETS pilots, polluter pays) vs information (AQI). NCAP cities, stubble, brick kilns, vehicular, waste burning.
Water: BOD, untreated sewage, industrial clusters, Namami Gange as governance not slogan.

environment.title: Climate: mitigation and adaptation
explain: Mitigation: energy, forests (carbon sink debates), methane, industry. Adaptation: floods, heat action plans, seeds, insurance, resilient housing. Bihar is adaptation-heavy.
Loss and damage, climate finance, CBDR-RC are the international politics layer.

environment.title: EIA and federal green clearance
explain: Screening, scoping, public hearing, appraisal, post-clearance monitoring. Exemptions and violations are the newspaper file. NGT and SC overlay.
Development vs environment answers need a process, not a sermon.

ethics.title: Value cards
explain: Index cards: integrity, objectivity, empathy, perseverance, impartiality, public service, accountability. Front: your definition. Back: a 4-line Bihar or Union case.

ethics.title: Thinkers as tools, not wallpaper
explain: Gandhi: means–ends, trusteeship, satyagraha as truth-force. Kant: duty and treating persons as ends. Aristotle: golden mean. Mill: harm principle and utility — useful for policy trade-offs. Kautilya: danda with dharma; statecraft without celebrating cruelty.
One thinker per answer, applied to the fact pattern.

ethics.title: Attitude, aptitude, EI
explain: Attitude: ABC (affect, behaviour, cognition) and how training plus leadership changes it. Aptitude: foundational values of civil service (2nd ARC). EI: self-awareness, regulation, motivation, empathy, social skill — operational in a riot, flood camp, or angry counter.
Write a 6-line incident, not a textbook paragraph.

ethics.title: Probity toolkit
explain: Code of conduct vs ethics, RTI, asset disclosure, whistle-blower, citizen charter, social audit, e-procurement, conflict-of-interest recusal.
Corruption answers need prevention architecture, not only punishment rhetoric.

ethics.title: Case practice roster
explain: Weekly: flood relief targeting, teacher recruitment leak, contractor pressure, caste data and fairness, hospital referral refusal, social media by a civil servant.
Always: facts → stakeholders → options (including delay) → constitutional values → chosen path + communication + monitoring.
